slides.title: A function with yield
slides.sub: A call creates a generator and runs nothing
slides.main: return gives and ends; yield gives and pauses, keeping all state.

body.text:
def countdown(n):
    while n > 0:
        yield n
        n -= 1

g = countdown(3)
print(type(g).__name__)
print(next(g), next(g), next(g))
print(list(countdown(2)))

slides.title: Order of execution
slides.sub: Inside code runs only as far as values are requested
slides.main: Interleaved execution of two programs, caller and generator, is the essence.

body.text:
def gen():
    print("start")
    yield 1
    print("middle")
    yield 2
    print("end")

g = gen()
print("created")
print(next(g))
print(next(g))
try:
    next(g)
except StopIteration:
    print("StopIteration")

slides.title: A generator is an iterator
slides.main: Need to go twice? Call the generator function again: each call is a new cursor.

body.text:
def squares(n):
    for i in range(n):
        yield i * i

g = squares(4)
print(list(g))
print(list(g))
print(sum(squares(4)), 9 in squares(4))

slides.title: Infinite generators
slides.main: No class, no stored sequence: values are born and forgotten.

slides.title: Generator expression
slides.main: Fold once into a number: expression; need a list to revisit: list comprehension.

body.text:
s = sum(x * x for x in range(1_000_000))
print(s)
gen = (x * x for x in range(3))
print(type(gen).__name__, list(gen))
A million squares, no list in memory.

slides.main: One element at a time flows through: a 100 GB file like a 100 KB one.

slides.title: send: values inside
slides.main: The basis of coroutines and async: a function pauses and yields control.

body.text:
def averager():
    total, n = 0, 0
    avg = None
    while True:
        x = yield avg
        total += x
        n += 1
        avg = total / n

g = averager()
next(g)               # reached the first yield
print(g.send(10), g.send(20), g.send(30))

slides.title: Context managers
slides.main: Before yield is entering with, after is leaving; try/finally ensures cleanup on error.

slides.title: Typical techniques
slides.main: The consumer ignores the source's structure; the source ignores why values are needed.

slides.title: Common mistakes
slides.sub: A generator does nothing until asked
slides.main: The criterion is clarity: rewrite a complex expression as a function with yield.

body.text:
def gen():
    print("not printed without next")
    yield 1

g = gen()               # nothing executed
print("created")
print(list(g), list(g))
Also: second pass over a generator, unlimited infinite one, return with a value inside a generator.
